subject: Request for evidence: customer opt-out & no-train proof for LLM
messages:
From: Sara Lane <sara.lane@acmecloud.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Evidence request — confirmation of opt-out / no-train for customer data

Hi Tessa,

We're preparing a GDPR compliance packet for an internal review and need explicit evidence from Redwood that Acme Cloud customer interactions processed through your hosted inference service are not used to train or improve models (and the process for customers to opt out). Specifically we need:

- A short written confirmation of your default training policy for hosted customers (are prompts/responses used to train models by default?)
- The technical controls and isolation guarantees for Dedicated and Private deployments
- Audit evidence examples (log exports, retention settings, last access/processing timestamps) that demonstrate no training ingestion
- Any SCCS/CAIQ mapping or questionnaire evidence you can share that maps to these controls
- Contact for a short (30 min) walk-through by May 25 if we have follow-ups

Can you provide the above (or a timeline for delivery)? This is time-sensitive for our procurement review.

Thanks,
Sara Lane
Senior Privacy Counsel
Acme Cloud
privacy@acmecloud.com

Attachment: none
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lane <sara.lane@acmecloud.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Evidence request — confirmation of opt-out / no-train for customer data

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. We can provide all of this. High level up front:

- Redwood DOES NOT use customer prompts/responses to train our base models by default for hosted paid customers. Training on customer data is explicitly opt-in and only performed under specific contracts and controls.
- Dedicated and Private deployments provide stronger isolation: Dedicated uses tenant-separated GPU pools and does not route content to our shared training pipelines; Private (VPC/on-prem) keeps all inference data in customer-controlled networks.

I'm attaching a concise process document that outlines the "no-train" workflow, evidence artifacts we can produce, and expected timelines. Ben will attach SCCS mapping and logs; Karthik will confirm any product-specific isolation notes for Dedicated.

We can deliver the requested artifacts by EOD May 20 and schedule a 30-minute walkthrough on May 23 or 24. Does May 23 @ 11am PT work?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
T: +1 415 555 0123
E: tessa_morgan@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-no-train-process.pdf (summary, 3 pages)

Team — forwarding Acme's request. Quick asks: 

- Ben: can you generate a SCCS/CAIQ mapping focused on no-train controls and export the relevant retention/log examples (anonymized) we can share? They asked for logs showing no ingestion into any training pipeline.
- Karthik: confirm the technical separation for Dedicated pools (routing, KV cache handling, snapshot/backup retention) so we can state explicit guarantees.
- Marissa: can you draft a one-page customer-facing statement we can send them as formal attestation?

Goal: produce artifacts by EOD May 20. If any blocker, call out now.

Thanks — T

Subject: RE: Acme — SCCS mapping & logs (no-train)

Tessa — attaching the requested mapping and a short note on available artifacts.

Attachments: sccs-mapping.csv (mapping rows for control families relevant to training/ingestion), sample-log-export.txt (anonymized event set)

Summary of what we can provide now:
- SCCS/CAIQ mapping that highlights controls covering data segregation, customer opt-out, model training pipelines, and logging/forensics. See attached CSV.
- A sanitized log export showing inference request metadata and that there is no pipeline ingestion event type present for these tenant IDs. (We redact any user-identifying fields.)
- A one-page attestation draft (Marissa will finalise) that states Redwood's default policy and the contractual opt-in requirement for training.

Notes on technical isolation (quick):
- Hosted (default): requests are processed by our shared serving runtime. We do NOT automatically forward request/response content to training pipelines. Prefix caching and KV cache are ephemeral unless explicitly configured for longer retention by the customer.
- Dedicated: tenant-separated GPU pools + isolated queues. We do not expose training pipelines to Dedicated queues by policy and default routing rules.
- Private: control plane can be configured to never export any inference data to Redwood-managed training systems.

If Acme needs signed artifacts we can provide an exec-signed attestation and a short live walkthrough of logs and controls.

Ben

Subject: RE: Evidence request — confirmation of opt-out / no-train for customer data

Sara — attaching the artifacts Ben referenced and a short attestation. Summary answers below (short and concrete):

1) Do you train on customer prompts/responses by default?- No. Redwood does not use customer prompts/responses from hosted paid accounts to train base models by default. Training on customer data occurs only under explicit, contractually-scoped opt-in.

2) How can a customer opt out?- Hosted: opt-out is the default (no training). If a customer has an exceptional opt-in clause, it is documented in the order form and executed only after security review.
- Dedicated: routing rules and tenant isolation prevent automatic ingestion; customers may enable extra telemetry only under explicit config.
- Private: customers control data flow. Redwood will not enable export paths to training systems unless explicitly requested and documented.

3) Evidence we are providing (attachments):
- redwood-no-train-process.pdf — description of operational process and the "no-train" default (attaches to this thread).
- sccs-mapping.csv — CSV mapping CAIQ/SIG rows to our controls and evidence locations.
- sample-log-export.txt (shared in secure drive) — anonymized request metadata showing no ingestion events for sample tenant IDs.

We can also provide an exec-signed attestation if needed and schedule a 30-minute walkthrough to share the log export and demonstrate the routing/queue separation. Proposed time: May 23, 11am PT. Please confirm or propose alternatives.

Thanks for the review. If you need anything more specific (signed attestation, DPIA excerpt), flag it and we'll prioritize.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
